name: Trie (Prefix Tree)
description: A Trie is a tree-like data structure used to store a dynamic set of strings. Unlike binary search trees, no node stores the key associated with that node; instead, its position in the tree defines the key. It enables efficient prefix-based searches and is ideal for autocomplete and dictionary implementations.
how_it_works: Each node represents a character, and paths from root to nodes form strings. Nodes have children for each possible next character. Leaf nodes or special markers indicate complete words. Insertion traverses/creates character nodes. Search follows character path. Prefix search can enumerate all words under a node.

complexity.time: O(m) for insert/search where m is string length
complexity.space: O(ALPHABET_SIZE * N * m) worst case, O(N) average with compression

key_parameters: case_sensitivity: treat 'A' and 'a' as same or different
compression: use compressed/radix tries to save space
max_depth: limit search depth for autocomplete
top_k_results: number of suggestions to return
pseudocode_or_diagram_description: Insert(word): node = root. For each char c in word: if c not in node.children: node.children[c] = new Node. node = node.children[c]. Mark node as end-of-word. Search(word): node = root. For each char c in word: if c not in node.children: return false. node = node.children[c]. Return node.is_end. Prefix search: traverse to prefix node, then DFS/BFS to collect all words below.
